rv.q: CADEL: Lungs on Legs showcases a rare fusion of sport and theatre which appeals both to the hardcore fans and the uninformed in equal measure.

The show will bring back wonderful memories for cycling fans, inject some much missed sun into the lives of ex-pat Aussies facing into the English winter and offer a unique theatrical experience for those who want to see a good story told with heart, mind and, yes, lungs too.
The show has won awards and garnered many five-star reviews from others, and it is very well staged, well-acted, and never dull.
It is an innovative and moving combination of genres that deserves all of the recognition it has already had.
CADEL: Lungs On Legs is an inventive, physically demanding and heartfelt piece of theatre that proves a compelling story doesn't need bells and whistles.
It is informative, entertaining, charming and inspirational.
It is an amazing performance and exhausting to watch.
This Tour de France tale is a triumphant Tour de Force.
All in all this is a slick, well performed show which deserves a successful run in London - and a tour beyond.
This is pitch-perfect theatre-making that manages to be utterly clear, technically brilliant and emotionally compelling all at the same time.
This is a truly packed show that condenses the heart and grit of this legendary story, brimming with personal touches and delivered with the commitment of a bike-throw photo finish.

cn.t: Critics praise this exhilarating one-man show, with Connor Delves delivering a physically demanding performance while cycling throughout. The production successfully blends athletic endurance with compelling storytelling about cyclist Cadel Evans.
